correctness.rationale: All smooth parameters \(t^2\ne1\) give six-point simply branched covers of smooth elliptic \(E\) and genus four. Two exact independent symbolic implementations compute the complete Hasse–Witt matrices: in characteristic five \(\operatorname{diag}(0,0,0,t^2-2)\) and in characteristic seven \(\operatorname{diag}(3,3t^3-2t,0,t^3-2t)\). Semilinear diagonal Frobenius has stable rank equal to its matrix rank. The elliptic Hasse invariant is zero or three at these primes, respectively, and the degree-two Prym isogeny preserves \(p\)-divisible groups for odd \(p\). Polynomial zero loci and all rank and \(a\)-number rows follow exactly, not by partial enumeration.

Its Section 5 specifically identifies Prym arithmetic as a meaningful direction. value.rationale: The cyclic order-six one-parameter nonhyperelliptic genus-four double-elliptic locus has motivated exact arithmetic invariants relevant to the paper’s explicit question on Prym superspeciality. The first two prime-characteristic complete coefficient stratifications yield a characteristic-seven superspecial Prym over an ordinary E with a nonsuperspecial J(C), outside the literature’s superspecial full-Jacobian census. The whole locus is classified, not an arbitrary isolated coefficient or a known-table recomputation; isomorphism counts and broader generalizations are not claimed.
